rationale: Cinematic still captures the decisive moment of a price split in a real home setting rather than a sterile studio. The split-screen diptych makes the two price paths legible at a glance, preserving the article's core factory-versus-brand tension.
cue: two near-identical machines on two different price paths
subject: two identical unbranded robot mowers on a concrete driveway, separated by a painted customs boundary line
core_thesis: A proposed 45.6% to 53.3% duty on Chinese-built robot mowers turns customs origin into the price variable, splitting otherwise identical machines onto two different price paths.
core_conflict: Customs origin versus shelf price: the same badge can sell at two different prices depending on which factory bolted the frame together, and the only readable clue is the price itself.
composition: split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast
